# Daniel 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** During the third year of King Jehoiakim's reign in Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

**2** The Lord allowed him to defeat King Jehoiakim and to carry off some of the sacred objects from the Temple of God. He took them to Babylonia and put them in the treasury of his god's temple.

**3** Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, his chief of staff, to bring some of the young men of Israel's royal family and nobility to the palace —

**4** Young men who were healthy, handsome, intelligent, well-educated, quick learners, and qualified to serve in the king's palace. They were to be taught the language and literature of Babylon.

**5** The king assigned them a daily serving of the food and wine from his own table. They were to be trained for three years, after which they would enter the king's service.

**6** Among those chosen were four young men from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

**7** The chief of staff renamed them: Daniel was called Belteshazzar, Hananiah was called Shadrach, Mishael was called Meshach, and Azariah was called Abednego.

**8** But Daniel made up his mind not to defile himself by eating the king's food or drinking his wine. He asked the chief of staff for permission to eat other things instead.

**9** God had given the chief of staff both respect and sympathy for Daniel,

**10** But he told Daniel, "I'm afraid of my lord the king. He's the one who decided what you should eat and drink. If he sees that you look worse than the other young men your age, he'll have my head!"

**11** So Daniel spoke to the attendant who had been assigned to look after Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

**12** "Please test us for ten days on a diet of vegetables and water," Daniel said.

**13** "At the end of ten days, compare us with the young men who eat from the king's table. Then decide what to do with us based on what you see."

**14** The attendant agreed to test them for ten days.

**15** At the end of the ten days, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better nourished than any of the young men who had been eating the king's food.

**16** So from then on, the attendant gave them vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.

**17** God gave these four young men exceptional ability in every area of literature and learning. And God gave Daniel a special ability to interpret visions and dreams.

**18** When the training period set by the king was over, the chief of staff brought all the young men before King Nebuchadnezzar.

**19** The king talked with each of them, and no one impressed him as much as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king's service.

**20** In every matter of wisdom and understanding the king tested them on, he found them ten times more capable than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.

**21** Daniel remained in the king's service until the first year of King Cyrus.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **1:2**: The most alarming verse in the chapter isn't about Daniel — it's 'the Lord gave' Israel's king to Babylon. God is behind the exile. That reframes everything.

- **1:8**: Daniel draws a line — not over learning Babylonian literature, not over getting a new name, but over food. It seems small, but it's about maintaining identity when everything else has been stripped away.

- **1:20**: Ten times better. Not marginally better — dramatically better. The message: faithfulness to God doesn't hold you back in a foreign culture; it propels you forward.

— PNEUMA
